clue.text: Treasured detective, Ramotswe

definitions.meaning: something treasured is valued and held dear
Alexander McCall Smith's Botswana detective, Mma Ramotswe, has this first name

explanation.walkthrough: Ramotswe runs The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency in Alexander McCall Smith's novels; her first name doubles as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precious is valued highly, and it is also the given name of Mma Ramotswe, the fictional detective.

clue.text: Managed a few children's books: that's one thing he did

definitions.text: children's books: that's one thing he did

parts.note: managed, as in ran a business, gives RAN
a few means some

explanation.surface: A remark about an author who managed a handful of children's books.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons and its sequels; the definition is a description of what he did, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome is the English writer of the Swallows and Amazons series for young readers.

clue.text: Scott's second smooth and piratical Captain, Clement

indicators.note: second points to the second letter of the word Scott's

parts.note: a smooth surface is level

explanation.surface: Sir Walter Scott's smooth-talking pirate captain named Clement.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scott's novel The Pirate the buccaneer is Captain Clement Cleveland; 'Scott's second' gives C, not a second novel by Scott.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Cleveland is the buccaneer captain in Walter Scott's novel The Pirate.

clue.text: Who falls for Cesario's country but not its capital

indicators.note: its capital here means its capital letter, the first one, which is dropped

parts.note: Bolivia is a South American country

explanation.surface: A riddle about a country without its capital city, set beside Shakespeare's disguised page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like La Paz or Sucre, but it is Bolivia's capital letter B. In Twelfth Night Viola disguises herself as the page Cesario, and the countess falls for her.
explanation.definitionFit: In Twelfth Night the countess Olivia falls in love with Cesario, who is Viola in disguise.

clue.text: Closet drama sonatas some sing incorrectly

indicators.note: sung incorrectly suggests the letters come out in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that some sonatas are being sung badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' rearranges SONATAS SOME SING into Milton's work. A closet drama is a play meant to be read rather than staged.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's verse tragedy about the blinded Hebrew strongman was written to be read, not performed, the mark of a closet drama.

clue.text: Snowbell's family is not large

definitions.meaning: Snowbell is the cat owned by the family of the mouse Stuart in E. B. White's book

explanation.walkthrough: Snowbell is the family cat in E. B. White's Stuart Little.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuart's adoptive family in E. B. White's story bear this surname, which also means small.

clue.text: What's left of pen used up padding stories

indicators.note: padding means the outer word is filled out with the other

parts.note: stories are lies, as in telling stories

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a pen for animals is a cage

explanation.surface: What is left of a pen once its ink is used up and it has been padding out tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is an animal enclosure; in a down clue 'used up' means written upwards, and 'padding' means it fills the stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Legacies are bequests, the things left to heirs after a death.

clue.text: Short story and song: Hermes is portrayed in these

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a story is a tale
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A short story and a song about the messenger god of Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts TALE to TAL. Hermes is shown in art with winged sandals on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Talaria are the winged sandals that Hermes wears in classical art.

clue.text: Rogue hampering a knight loyal to Henry V

definitions.text: a knight loyal to Henry V

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wayward, so the letters go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain obstructing a faithful knight of King Henry's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' rearranges HAMPERING. Sir Thomas Erpingham is the old knight who lends King Henry his cloak before Agincourt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Erpingham is the loyal old officer in Shakespeare's Henry V.

clue.text: In part revenge dictated where David hid from Saul

indicators.note: In part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A biblical tale of revenge that dictated where David hid from King Saul.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel 24 David hides in a cave at En-gedi, where he spares Saul's life.
explanation.definitionFit: The oasis of En-gedi by the Dead Sea is the wilderness refuge where David hid from Saul's pursuit.

clue.text: Processing unit's flag-waving in revolutionary ode

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the turned word
revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ode is a poem

indicators.note: a waving flag is moved about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Flag-waving inside a poem in praise of revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag-waving' suggests patriotism, but 'waving' only shuffles the flag; 'revolutionary' turns the ode round, and 'in' sets one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaflop is a measure of computing speed, a million floating-point operations per second.

clue.text: Victim of lago's fix in a Copland ballet

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

parts.note: Rodeo is a ballet score by Aaron Copland
to fix a result is to rig it

explanation.surface: Iago's scheme carried out within an American ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lago' is Iago, Othello's villain, printed with a lower-case L. Roderigo is the gull he fleeces and finally stabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderigo is the foolish Venetian whom Iago exploits and then kills in Othello.

clue.text: Greek boatman going after fish

indicators.note: after says the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: the char is a fish related to the trout
a machine that is going is on

explanation.surface: A Greek sailor setting off in pursuit of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Charon ferries the souls of the dead across the river Styx.

clue.text: Writer Eden Paul's wife cared about

indicators.note: about means moved round, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: The wife of the writer Eden Paul looked after him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CARED. Eden and Cedar Paul were a married couple who translated many European books into English.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedar Paul was the wife and translating partner of the writer Eden Paul.

clue.text: Earl traitorous to Henry V caught by a village regularly on the radio

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Ambridge is the fictional village of The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap

explanation.surface: A traitor caught in a village that keeps cropping up on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal but just means the village is heard often. Ambridge is the home of BBC Radio 4's The Archers.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard, Earl of Cambridge, plots against the king and is executed in Shakespeare's Henry V.

clue.text: Zone a salesman has, formerly where Elijah visited a widow

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
hath is the old form of has

explanation.surface: A biblical journey in which a travelling salesman visits a widow.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Kings 17 Elijah lodges with a widow at Zarephath and multiplies her meal and oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Zarephath is the Phoenician town where the prophet Elijah stayed with a poor widow.

clue.text: Colourful part in a Welsh town victory we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are spoken and the answer is what they sound like

parts.note: Harlech, a Welsh coastal town with a castle, plus win for a victory

explanation.surface: A colourful role in a victory celebration in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns HARLECH WIN into its soundalike. Harlequin is the masked clown of pantomime and commedia, and the word also means many-coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is a stage role, the clown in a diamond-patched costume, and the word also describes bright multicoloured patterns.

clue.text: Patron saint of actors for all to see in a book

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

parts.note: Genesis is the first book of the Bible
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: An actors' patron saint shown publicly in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: A U certificate film is suitable for everyone in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Genesius, a Roman actor martyred by tradition, is honoured as protector of performers.

clue.text: A Jacobean playwright's core character, last to exit

parts.note: the core of something is its middle

indicators.note: last to exit means the final letter of the word departs

parts.note: the tone of a place is its character

explanation.surface: The central character in a Jacobean drama, the last to leave the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to exit' cuts TONE to TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Middleton wrote The Changeling and Women Beware Women in the reign of James I.

clue.text: Welshman drinking French wine cold — Genius!

indicators.note: drinking means the first piece takes the second into itself

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name in crosswords
vin is the French word for wine
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A Welshman downing chilled French wine is hailed a genius.
explanation.walkthrough: Dai is the stock Welsh name in crosswords; 'drinking' means the Welshman holds the wine inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci is the archetypal universal genius of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Folklorist's grave visited by millions

parts.note: grave as an adjective means grim
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A folklorist's grave is visited by huge numbers of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected German folk tales.

clue.text: Stretch out parts to a greater extent for a French dramatist

indicators.note: parts means the second piece splits the first open

parts.note: more means to a greater extent
to stretch out on a bed is to lie

explanation.surface: An instruction to stretch out the parts further for a French playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch out' and 'parts' read as one instruction, but 'parts' is the container signal, splitting the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the seventeenth-century French comic playwright of Tartuffe.

clue.text: Evergreen performer seen by Hardy

definitions.meaning: the bay tree is an evergreen shrub
Stan was the comic partner of Oliver Hardy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests Thomas Hardy, but it is Oliver Hardy of the film double act.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay is an evergreen of this name, and Stan of the name was Oliver Hardy's screen partner.

clue.text: Pay homage to Longfellow's rider

definitions.meaning: to pay homage is to honour or venerate
Paul, the silversmith whose midnight ride Longfellow's poem celebrates

explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow's poem Paul Revere's Ride tells of the 1775 night ride to warn of British troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to venerate, and Paul Revere is the horseman of Longfellow's poem.

clue.text: "Very virtuous maid" is a loose label

indicators.note: a loose label comes apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quoted description of a chaste girl is called a careless label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges IS A LABEL. In Measure for Measure Isabella, a novice nun, is called a very virtuous maid.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is the chaste novice of Measure for Measure, described as a very virtuous maid.

clue.text: Heretical Christian actor who played Mr Chips on screen first

parts.words: actor who played Mr Chips on screen
parts.note: Robert Donat won an Oscar playing Mr Chips in the 1939 film
first abbreviates to 1st, read as IST

explanation.surface: An actor known for playing Mr Chips on film comes first among heretics.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of 1st is read as the letter I. Goodbye, Mr Chips (1939) starred Robert Donat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Donatists were a schismatic North African Christian sect condemned as heretics by the Catholic church.

clue.text: John Edgar Wideman novel about a trap used by plumbers mostly

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: a U-bend is the water trap in a drain pipe

explanation.surface: A novel about a trap that plumbers use in most jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts UBEND to UBEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Reuben is a 1987 novel by the American writer John Edgar Wideman.

clue.text: English team against the French, making Joyce play

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team
les is the French plural for the

explanation.surface: An English team plays against France, staging a work by Joyce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' and 'making' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiles is James Joyce's only surviving stage play, from 1918.

clue.text: US author a large soprano embraces

indicators.note: embraces means the first piece wraps round the others

parts.note: a soprano is a singer

explanation.surface: A big soprano hugs an American writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts AL inside SINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger was the American novelist of The Catcher in the Rye.
